# Derived by tools/asynccheck.py - do not edit by hand; run it with --accept.
# Each line is a global written after an await with no check between the two.
# Being here means somebody read it and decided it is safe. It should shrink;
# when it grows, the run says so and the commit says which of the two reasons.
#
# The 17 entries added on 24 August came from the check *seeing more*, not from new debt: the two
# diagram windows ran their whole startup inside `(async function init() {…})()` and both settings
# pages ran nine handlers inside `onclick = async () => {…}`, and a scope that is not a declaration
# is one this tool cannot enter. They are named now. Read, and safe, for two reasons worth stating
# because neither is visible from the line:
#
#   `init` in either graphview - a one-shot startup with no competing writer. The window is opened
#   for one workspace and nothing else runs while it loads, so there is no second operation for a
#   guard to distinguish it from. DATA, N, ids, erP, drawMax, curFocus, egoDepth.
#
#   `_crmFrameSeen` in `crmFrameId` - the instrument's own line, written after the enumeration it
#   describes. It is a *record of what just happened*, not state anybody acts on, and a later
#   enumeration overwriting an earlier one is the record doing its job. Named here because a write
#   after an await is a write after an await, and an instrument is not exempt from the check it
#   exists to feed.
#
#   `onWsdel` in the CRM panel - the delete of the selected workspace. `currentPath = null` and the
#   preview closing land after the folder has been removed; a workspace switched to meanwhile would
#   have its preview closed, which is cosmetic and is followed by `loadWorkspaces()` anyway. Named
#   here because the guard at the top of the function is checked once, before the awaits, which is
#   the shape this repository records as protecting the first effect only - it happens not to matter
#   at this site, and that is a judgement rather than a property.
#
#   `onAiengine` / `onSaveAi` in either options page - **the settings page has no workspace**. It
#   holds no folder handle and no org, so the class this check is about - a value published into a
#   workspace that has since changed - has nothing to be wrong about here. Each write takes the
#   value the same operation just computed from the control it read after the await.
# The 24 lines added on 22 August 2026 are the options pages, the backgrounds and the content
# scripts, which this check had never read - `sidepanel.html` was its whole subject, 9 of the 32
# shipped scripts. The content scripts were *opened* and not read: both are wrapped in an IIFE, so
# every function in them is indented by two, and this tool looked at column zero - 0 of 32 and 0 of
# 19, over 42 awaits, in the two files that do the authenticated fetching. Corrected 22 August 2026,
# and the headline now prints how much of its own subject it read. What follows was true of the
# scopes it *did* read: none is the defect this tool is for, since
# that defect is «the *workspace* changed under an operation» and none of those scopes has one. What
# they have is one load overtaking another, and this line used to say the options pages «answer
# with markOwn/dirty». They did not: `markOwn` says «this change was mine, ignore the echo» and
# `dirty` says «I have unsaved edits», and neither orders two reads of one key. Measured on
# 23 August 2026 and answered with a token, `beginLoad(key)`, which shrank this ledger by 18.
# A note beside a ledger line is read as the reason nobody has to look again, so a wrong one
# costs more than none.
# Recorded rather than exempted, so a *new* one there is still a finding.
#
# The six in `saveKeys` are that writer's own bookkeeping and are after the await *on purpose*:
# they are what the write turned out to be. `markOwn` still runs before it, because the echo can
# arrive first; everything that is a claim about the outcome runs after, and on a refusal the
# mark is withdrawn and the key goes back to dirty.
#
# The three in `rebuildTree` are cache invalidations after the permission await: dropping a cache in
# the workspace you have left costs a rebuild, and the publication two lines below is guarded.
#
# What it cannot see is in the docstring: an arrow-function body, including the onChanged handler
# where both panels rewrite the folder handle after an await.
